task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's regression test (test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/entity_event_type_seeding_test.exs) for ISS-0721. Verify: (1) both acceptance criteria from lib/letflow/design/iss0721-entity-event-type-seeding.md section 6 are actually covered (fresh-tenant entity-record write succeeds without manual seed!/1; second-call idempotency); (2) the fail-first proof is real -- independently reproduce at least the fail side yourself (a throwaway git worktree of origin/main with only the new test file copied in, run it, confirm the same {:error, :unknown_event_type} failure TEST-DESIGNER reported) rather than accepting the reported counts as given, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's 'every producing step has a validating step' principle and this run's own worked-example precedent; (3) the test is isolated and self-sufficient (no cross-test state dependency); (4) triage the MINOR issue TEST-DESIGNER flagged (Letflow.Engine.Lua.PlatformTest/REQ-161 flaking under full-suite parallel load, 2/360, unrelated files) -- confirm it really is pre-existing/unrelated to this diff (e.g. check whether it's a known flake already on file, such as ISS-0723's SandboxPoolTest-class recurring flake pattern) and state in your result whether it should be filed as a fresh issue or is already tracked, per ORCHESTRATOR.md's decision-tree rule for incidental findings (file it, do not extend this run).
acceptance_criteria: Both design-doc AC's (fresh-tenant write succeeds, second-call idempotency) independently confirmed covered by the test file's actual assertions
Fail-first proof independently reproduced (at minimum the fail side, via your own throwaway worktree run), not merely accepted from the report
Incidental Lua/PlatformTest flake triaged and a disposition stated (already-tracked vs needs filing)
PASS or FAIL with specific findings

result.summary:
AC coverage (read test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/entity_event_type_seeding_test.exs directly, cross-checked against design doc section 6, not TEST-DESIGNER's summary): AC1 (fresh-tenant write succeeds without manual seed!/1) is covered by test 1 (lines 143-180) -- provisioned_tenant_no_manual_seed/0 (lines 66-99) provisions via provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/1 with no migration_source and deliberately omits any EventTypes.seed!/1 call (confirmed by reading the fixture body); the test then asserts Registry.get_type/2 == {:ok,_} for all 3 ENTITY_RECORD_* names AND drives real writes through Records.create_record/2, update_record/2, delete_record/2 (the stronger, production-path assertion the design's section 6 item 3 explicitly required over a get_type-only check). AC2 (second-call idempotency) is covered by test 2 (lines 182-193) -- calls replay_migrations/2 a second time against the same tenant_id, asserts {:ok,_}, then a real create_record/2 write still succeeds, exercising design section 4's 'seed!/1 already tolerates duplicates internally' claim. Both criteria map to real, non-vacuous assertions.

Fail-first proof, independently reproduced myself (not accepted from the report): `git worktree add ../letflow-iss0721-validate origin/main` (origin/main verified at ffc433d2, matching the spec's cited pre-fix tip, via `git rev-parse origin/main`), copied only test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/entity_event_type_seeding_test.exs into the worktree (test/support/sandbox_auto_mode.ex already exists on main, no other file needed), `mix deps.get`, then `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/entity_event_type_seeding_test.exs`. My own run:
```
  2) test ... the three ENTITY_RECORD_* event types are registered ...
     match (=) failed
     code:  assert {:ok, _type} = Registry.get_type(event_type, tenant_id)
     left:  {:ok, _type}
     right: {:error, :unknown_event_type}
Finished in 3.6 seconds (0.00s async, 3.6s sync)
Result: 0/2 passed
Failed: 2 tests
```
Matches TEST-DESIGNER's reported failure exactly (same error, same 0/2, same shape on both tests). Worktree removed afterward: `git worktree remove ../letflow-iss0721-validate --force`, confirmed via `git worktree list` showing only the main working tree. Also re-ran on this branch post-fix as a sanity check: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/entity_event_type_seeding_test.exs` -> `Result: 2 passed`, confirming the same file genuinely flips from fail to pass across the fix commit.

Test isolation: each test calls provisioned_tenant_no_manual_seed/0 independently, which creates its own tenant via a unique slug (Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1) and its own schema, with an on_exit callback that drops the schema and deletes both the Registration and Tenant rows -- no shared fixture state, no ordering dependency between the two tests, async: false is scoped to real-Postgres provisioning (not a cross-test hazard). No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' language, no hardcoded secrets or connection strings (DB access goes through Letflow.Repo/DataCase as everywhere else in this suite).

Incidental Lua/PlatformTest flake triage: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'platform_test.exs', 'PlatformTest', 'REQ-161', 'Lua.Platform' -- only ISS-0418 matches (wasm_hang concurrency-cap issue, a wasmex/native-thread-pool mechanism in test/letflow/engine/wasm/, unrelated file class, already resolved). Read ISS-0723.yaml in full: that is a DIFFERENT recurring flake class (Letflow.SandboxPoolTest 'RT-6 death path c', release-timeout pattern in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs/lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex) -- not the same test module, not the same mechanism (bounded-poll-deadline vs. Lua script-failure assertion timing under parallel load), so it does not cover this finding either. No existing docs/issues/ record tracks Letflow.Engine.Lua.PlatformTest (REQ-161) flaking under the full 16-partition parallel suite. Disposition: NOT already tracked -- needs filing as a fresh issue. Per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's procedure, the id must come from letflow-queue's register_task (never scanned/incremented locally), which only ORCH calls -- so this validator reports the finding in result.issues below (title, description, severity, affected_files) for ORCH to register and file, rather than fabricating an ISS-NNNN filename itself. Do not extend this run to investigate or fix the flake, per ORCHESTRATOR.md's decision-tree rule for incidental findings.

Overall verdict: PASS. Both design-doc acceptance criteria are genuinely covered by real, non-vacuous assertions; the fail-first proof is independently reproduced (not merely trusted); the test is isolated and self-sufficient; the incidental flake is triaged with a clear disposition (needs filing, not a duplicate of any tracked issue).
